--- page 1 ---
Results
Participants studied word lists of different lengths and then recalled as many words as they could.
As Figure 1 shows, recall fell steadily as the lists grew longer.
The pattern held for every age group we tested.
Table 1 lists the mean number of words recalled in each condition.
Longer lists also produced more intrusions, which we discuss below.
--- page 2 ---
Recall was best for words at the start and end of each list.
These results match the classic serial position effect.
